answer: Zero-knowledge proofs and verifiable delay functions impose a sequential exponentiation chain of length L that forces any prover to spend deterministic time T before a valid credential appears. Each identity stakes collateral C and incurs slashing penalty S proportional to C on premature output, yielding negative expected utility and a very robust Nash equilibrium reinforced by the ripple of forced delay, the pulse of periodic audits, and the jetty of immutable commitments.
